mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signals a disinflationary environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real earnings growth improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where CPIAUCSL declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate robust consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) both increase by more than 5% in a month, it signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher economic activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals an accommodative monetary policy with inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate continued low rates and economic growth.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with inflationary pressures
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL is rising.
